title: Make the reader state which agent roles a "Athena knows X" request
summary: Root cause (class knowledge-request-read-as-docs-for-humans-not-agent-behavior, 20261109-091813-hhqq): the reader prompt never makes the reader decide whether "Athena should know/act on X" means docs or agent behavior, nor list the rules that bound the affected role. Fix it in crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, within the 71-token reader budget, with a test on the composed prompt. The audience is the reader role, plus the verifiers who judge its readings. Retries 20261109-080749-p0fs and 20261109-080220-zkhy.

defaults_applied.how: The fix is in the reader prompt that produced both misreadings, not in either job's output.
A test on the composed reader prompt, plus fmt, clippy and the whole test suite.
The test checks the composed prompt text the reader actually receives.
One rule in one prompt file, within the token budget.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, where the reader rules live. crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs compose it as READER_FRAME. Prompt edits are mirror-checked by crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs. The change adds no record or data file, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not involved. The budget is measured directly by composing the real prompt.
Term ladder: the ordered rungs of change size or authority that cap what a role may decide, per docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md; a rung limit is one of the rules the reader must list.

Fixing at the reader prompt matches both introspections' proposals. The steward-side failures in job 20261109-080220-zkhy and the README failure in 20261109-080749-p0fs are instances; their code and doc candidates are not kept.
The prompt edit may need a docs/decisions.md entry, so it is listed with moderate probability.
Placing the rule in defaults.toml was rejected: it is a governance file, and the reader budget counts defaults too.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md gains one rule in 'Reading the request': when a request says Athena or its agents should know, understand or act on something, the reading must state whether it means docs or agent behavior, name the roles and prompts that change, list the rules that bound those roles (ladder rungs, budgets, role limits, admission rules) and list as deliverables any blocking rule that is not owner-only. Verify with git diff.

A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs asserts the composed reader prompt contains the docs-versus-agent-behavior rule and the rule-listing requirement. It fails on the pre-change reader.md and passes after. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.

The budget check in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs still passes: the reader set stays at or under 2000 tokens (71 left), so the producer must trim existing reader.md words if needed. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets.

The change description (CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]) names the root cause, the ambiguity between docs for readers and built-in agent behavior, and says the fix is in the reader prompt, not in jobs 20261109-080749-p0fs or 20261109-080220-zkhy. Their candidates' README.md, CHANGELOG.md and steward changes are dropped, so the verifier can check the prior findings do not recur in the diff.
Mirror and policy checks pass for the prompt edit: cargo test (whole workspace), including athena-core mirrors tests and the xtask policy test, plus cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy, all pass.

No new refusal rule is added; the change is prose-only, marked as such in CHANGELOG.md. It does not edit defaults.toml, athena.toml or workflows, which Athena changes only via its proposal path, so no past readings are newly refused (expected 0% of newly refused readings).

out_of_scope: README.md, docs/architecture.md and the steward prompt or code (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs, crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs, crates/athena-data/src/records.rs): the earlier candidates are dropped
defaults.toml, athena.toml, workflows, BRIEF.md and records/
A code check that refuses readings
urgent_reason: It cuts repeated rejected attempts: the same misreading failed two jobs, and each failure cost a redo.
hard_reason: It changes the reader prompt, the step that shapes how every job is read and planned, so a mistake affects all later jobs.
